name: Executive Order of January 28, 1876 defining the Malheur Reservation (the reservation itself, Royce areas 638 and 646)
nations: Wadatika and other Snake or Paiute bands of the Malheur country (Northern Paiute), today the Burns Paiute Tribe
promises: Not a treaty: a presidential order. It superseded the order of May 15, 1875 and set apart a new reserve on the Malheur River bounded by Castle Rock, Strawberry Butte, Silvies Creek, Malheur Lake and the South Fork of the Malheur (Royce p. 884).

Royce says this reserve was all of the original reserve of September 12, 1872 and part of the 1875 addition, and points to areas 638 and 646 and his note under the order of May 21, 1883 (Royce p. 885).
The Indian Claims Commission found the bands had exclusively used and occupied the land within these 1876 boundaries from time immemorial to January 1879 and never ceded it (finding 40).

breaches.what: The Commission found the bands were deprived of their title to the land within the boundaries of this order in January 1879, when the United States forcibly removed them to the Yakima Reservation and restored the land to the public domain without their consent or payment; the restoring orders of September 13, 1882 and May 21, 1883 followed, and none of the land was sold for their benefit.

landTaken: The Commission found the tract within the 1876 boundaries; its acreage figure is garbled in the scanned 1959 order and is left out.
compensation: The Commission valued the land at $579,722.00 as of January 1879, less offsets (Second Interlocutory Order, April 15, 1959). Interior described the judgment as $567,000 (press release, 1963).
today: The Burns Paiute Tribe lives near Burns, Oregon, on the edge of the former reservation. This is the same taking already recorded under cession-1872-09-12-paiute-shoshone-snake, cession-1872-09-12-paiute-shoshoni-snake, cession-1875-05-15-paiute-shoshoni and cession-1876-01-28-paiute-shoshoni; it is one taking (January 1879), not a new one.

nationVoice.summary: The Tribe says an executive order reservation of 1.8 million acres was short-lived: after the Bannock War its surviving ancestors were marched over 300 miles in deep snow to Fort Simcoe and Fort Vancouver, and the reservation was lost.

openQuestions: Do not re-count: this record and cession-1872-09-12-paiute-shoshone-snake both map Royce areas 638 and 646 (the reservation as restored in 1882 and 1883) and rest on the same Docket 17 finding, which is also used by cession-1872-09-12-paiute-shoshoni-snake, cession-1875-05-15-paiute-shoshoni and cession-1876-01-28-paiute-shoshoni. The finding is about this record's land (the reservation as defined by this very order), so the status stands, but the map should count one taking. Jordan may want these merged.

treaties.json errors: presentDayTribes is empty (the Burns Paiute Tribe should be listed); scheduleTribes reads "Paiute; Shoshone; Snake" while the Commission names Snake or Piute bands; a statute file (638c.pdf) is linked for what Royce lists as executive orders. Not edited.
The Burns Paiute page dates the reservation to 1869; Royce and the Commission give September 12, 1872 for the first order. Recorded as the Tribe's account.
The final judgment in Docket 17 and whether the judgment was distributed were not traced.
2026-11-08: counted once with cession-1872-09-12-paiute-shoshone-snake (an order on the Malheur reservation; the January 1879 taking of the reservation is counted once). The map still shows this row.

plain.promised: Not a treaty. A presidential order fixed the Malheur Reservation's boundaries for the Paiute bands, land the Indian Claims Commission later found they had always used and never gave up.
plain.happened: The Commission found that in January 1879 the United States forcibly removed the bands to Yakima and returned the land to the public domain without consent or payment. Interior admitted in 1963 no compensation was paid.
plain.today: The Commission valued the land at $579,722.00; Interior described a $567,000 judgment. This is the same taking shown on four other Malheur entries.
